newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma Yadana gas pipeline ready in three months.
newsitem.headline: Burma Yadana gas pipeline ready in three months.

text.p: The offshore pipeline for Burma's Yadana gas field will be completed in three months, the official Myanmar News Agency (MNA) reported on Friday.
The MNA said about 10 miles of the 216-mile long, 36-inch diameter pipeline have already been laid offshore. The remainder will be finished in three months.
About 40 miles of 39-inch diametere gas pipeline linking the shore and the Thai border have been laid onshore, it said.
The Burmese pipeline will connect with one being built on the Thai side in the border province of Kanchanaburi and on to a power station in central Ratchaburi province.
The Yadana project initially will provide 325 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas to Thailand in 1998. Under the 30-year contract, that will increase to 525 mmcfd in 1999.
Total production will reach 650 mmcfd, with 125 mmcfd being used domestically to operate a 300 megawatt power plant and a urea fertiliser plant with annual production capacity of 570,000 tonnes.
Yadana's gas in place is estimated at more than five trillion cubic feet.

PTT Exploration and Production Plc owns 25.5 percent of the field. Unocal of the United States has 28.26 percent, Total SA of France 31.24 percent and Burma's state-run Myanma Oil and Gas Enterprise 15 percent.
